title: CatalogSage — AI-Powered Product Catalog Assistant — Project Overview … Technologies
text:
## Project Overview
CatalogSage is an AI assistant designed to answer natural-language questions about an e-commerce product catalog containing more than 300 SKUs. It helps users find relevant product information without manually searching through catalog entries.

## Problem
Users may ask about products using descriptions rather than exact product names or identifiers. Simple keyword search may fail when the question wording differs from the catalog wording.

## Solution
The application combines an API backend, an AI workflow, retrieval, and catalog-service integrations to identify relevant product information and generate a useful response.

## Technologies
- Python, FastAPI
- LangGraph, OpenAI API
- Embeddings, BM25, hybrid retrieval
- MCP
- Docker, Kubernetes, Jenkins, Ansible

title: CatalogSage — AI-Powered Product Catalog Assistant — Architecture
text:
## Architecture
1. **User question:** The user submits a product-related question.
2. **Request processing:** The backend validates the request and identifies the required processing path.
3. **Retrieval:** The application searches the catalog. Semantic retrieval can find related content when wording differs; BM25 identifies relevant results using lexical term matching. A hybrid approach can combine these signals.
4. **Tool integration:** MCP can provide a standardized way for an AI application to interact with supported catalog tools or services. Tool access should be limited to required operations.
5. **Response generation:** The LLM uses retrieved product information to prepare a natural-language answer. It should not invent product specifications.
6. **Validation:** The application checks inputs and outputs and handles cases where relevant information cannot be found.

title: CatalogSage — AI-Powered Product Catalog Assistant — Why Combine Semantic Search and BM25? … Why LangGraph?
text:
## Why Combine Semantic Search and BM25?
Semantic search focuses on meaning and conceptual similarity. BM25 focuses on lexical overlap and term relevance. Combining them can help with descriptive questions and exact product terminology.

## Why LangGraph?
LangGraph supports explicit workflow steps and conditional routing. It is useful when the application needs different paths for different request types or needs to call tools before generating a response.

title: CatalogSage — AI-Powered Product Catalog Assistant — Interview Questions
text:
## Interview Questions
**What problem does CatalogSage solve?**  
It helps users find product information by asking natural-language questions instead of manually searching the catalog.

**Why use hybrid retrieval?**  
Semantic search helps with meaning, while BM25 helps with keyword matching. Combining them can improve retrieval across different types of questions.

**What is MCP?**  
The Model Context Protocol is a standard for connecting AI applications with external tools and data sources through defined interfaces.

**Why use FastAPI?**  
FastAPI provides a framework for building Python APIs, validating requests, and exposing backend functionality.

**What happens if the catalog does not contain the answer?**  
The application should indicate that the information is unavailable instead of inventing product specifications.

**How would you evaluate retrieval quality?**  
Create representative product questions with known relevant catalog entries. Measure whether correct entries appear in top results, using metrics such as Recall@k and MRR where appropriate.

The application aims to automate parts of this process while retaining validation and human review for uncertain results.

title: Clinical Document Intelligence and Structured Extraction — Proposed Processing Workflow › 2. PDF Processing …
text:
## Proposed Processing Workflow › 2. PDF Processing
PyMuPDF can extract text from PDFs that already contain a text layer and help inspect or split documents into pages. Scanned PDFs may require OCR because their pages contain images rather than directly extractable text.

## Proposed Processing Workflow › 3. OCR
Amazon Textract can extract text and supported document elements from scanned documents and images. The application can use the OCR response to obtain text and associated confidence information. OCR confidence does not prove that recognized text is medically correct.

## Proposed Processing Workflow › 4. Extraction
An LLM can transform extracted text into a predefined structured format, such as test name, reported value, unit, date, and source page. The model should not fill missing values with assumptions.

title: Clinical Document Intelligence and Structured Extraction — Proposed Processing Workflow › 5. Structured Valida
text:
## Proposed Processing Workflow › 5. Structured Validation
Pydantic can validate whether generated output follows the expected schema and data types. Additional rules can check date formats, allowed values, missing fields, and inconsistent records. Passing schema validation does not prove factual correctness.

## Proposed Processing Workflow › 6. Grounding and Evidence Verification
The application checks extracted values against source text and page references. Page and bounding-box information, where available, can help reviewers locate original content. A value should not be marked verified merely because the LLM returned valid JSON.

## Proposed Processing Workflow › 7. Human Review
Records with missing evidence, low OCR confidence, ambiguous handwriting, or conflicting values should be sent for review.

title: Clinical Document Intelligence and Structured Extraction — Proposed Processing Workflow › 8. Storage and API R
text:
## Proposed Processing Workflow › 8. Storage and API Response
Validated information can be stored in the configured database and returned through FastAPI. Access controls should protect sensitive clinical information.

## Why Amazon Textract?
Amazon Textract is a document-analysis service that extracts text and supported structural information from documents. It is useful for OCR workflows involving scanned documents, forms, and tables. Capabilities and quality depend on document type, language, handwriting, layout, and selected API.

## Why PyMuPDF?
PyMuPDF can extract existing PDF text, inspect page content, render pages, and support document splitting. It is useful before OCR because not every PDF requires text recognition.

## Why Pydantic?
Pydantic validates application data against defined models and types. It helps ensure extracted output follows the application's expected structure.

title: Clinical Document Intelligence and Structured Extraction — Why Use an LLM? … Why Is Human Review Necessary?
text:
## Why Use an LLM?
An LLM can interpret context and map extracted text into a predefined schema. Output must be checked because the model may omit information, misinterpret ambiguous text, or generate unsupported values.

## Why Is Grounding Important?
Grounding connects an extracted value or generated answer to evidence in the source document. This helps reviewers verify the correct value, date, unit, or test name.

## Why Is Human Review Necessary?
Some records are ambiguous or difficult to read. Human review handles uncertainty instead of automatically accepting potentially incorrect data.

title: Clinical Document Intelligence and Structured Extraction — Safety Considerations
text:
## Safety Considerations
- Do not invent missing clinical values.
- Preserve units and dates from the source.
- Flag conflicting values for review.
- Separate schema validity from factual correctness.
- Restrict access to sensitive documents.
- Minimize personal information sent to external models.
- Use appropriate encryption and access controls.
- Do not treat extracted data as a medical diagnosis.
- Retain source references so reviewers can verify output.

title: Clinical Document Intelligence and Structured Extraction — Interview Questions
text:
## Interview Questions
**What is the difference between PDF text extraction and OCR?**  
PDF text extraction reads text already embedded in the PDF. OCR recognizes text from page images, such as scanned documents.

**Why use Textract instead of a basic OCR library?**  
Textract is a managed document-analysis service with support for extracting text and certain structural elements. The choice depends on document quality, required features, cost, and language requirements.

**What does Pydantic validate?**  
It validates structure and types. Separate checks are needed to establish whether extracted values match the source.

**How do you handle unreadable handwriting?**  
Flag uncertain content for review rather than inventing a value.

**How do you prevent the LLM from inventing clinical values?**  
Use constrained extraction instructions, structured schemas, source evidence, deterministic validation, and human review for uncertain results.

**Does valid JSON mean the extraction is correct?**  
No. Valid JSON only shows that output follows the required structure. Extracted values must also be checked against the source.

**What is the difference between OCR confidence and extraction confidence?**  
OCR confidence relates to text recognition. Extraction confidence concerns how reliably a field was identified or interpreted. Neither alone proves correctness.

title: Clinical Document Intelligence and Structured Extraction — Interview Questions
text:
## Interview Questions
**How would you evaluate this system?**  
Compare extracted fields against manually verified reference data. Measure field-level precision and recall, exact-match accuracy where appropriate, schema validity, evidence support, and the proportion of fields requiring human review.

This project helps financial operations and compliance teams investigate B2B transactions through natural-language questions. Instead of manually searching multiple records, users can ask questions and receive responses based on relevant transaction data and supporting evidence.

## Problem
Financial investigations may require checking transaction records, applying business rules, reviewing supporting evidence, and understanding relationships between records. A basic chatbot may generate an answer without checking the underlying data, creating reliability risks.

## Solution
An agentic RAG application combines retrieval, backend tools, workflow orchestration, and validation to support financial investigations.

## Technologies

title: AI Compliance and Financial Operations Assistant — Architecture › 1. User Interface and API … Architecture › 4
text:
## Architecture › 1. User Interface and API
The user submits a natural-language question. FastAPI receives the request and performs required authentication and authorization checks.

## Architecture › 2. Workflow Orchestration
LangGraph manages the multi-step workflow. Depending on the question, the workflow can classify the request, select a path, invoke tools, process results, and prepare a response.

## Architecture › 3. Data Retrieval
The application retrieves relevant information from available data sources. PostgreSQL stores relational data, while pgvector supports vector-based similarity search where appropriate.

## Architecture › 4. Tool Execution
The workflow can call approved backend tools to retrieve transaction information or apply deterministic business rules. The LLM should not independently invent transaction facts; tool results and retrieved evidence provide the information used to construct the answer.

title: AI Compliance and Financial Operations Assistant — Architecture › 5. Response Generation … Why LangGraph?
text:
## Architecture › 5. Response Generation
The LLM uses available information to generate a natural-language response.

## Architecture › 6. Validation and Grounding
The application checks whether the response is supported by evidence and follows the expected output format. When evidence is insufficient, the system should avoid presenting unsupported conclusions as facts.

## Architecture › 7. Evaluation and Monitoring
Representative test cases can evaluate answer relevance, evidence usage, tool selection, and response correctness. Tracing and regression tests help identify problems introduced by changes to prompts, retrieval settings, or workflows.

## Why LangGraph?
LangGraph is useful when an AI application requires multiple steps, conditional routing, state management, tool execution, retries, or human intervention. A simple prompt may be sufficient for a straightforward question; a graph-based workflow is useful when explicit control is needed.

title: AI Compliance and Financial Operations Assistant — Why RAG? … Important Design Considerations
text:
## Why RAG?
RAG retrieves relevant information before generating an answer. It is useful when responses must reflect specific business records or domain knowledge that may not be contained in the model's training data.

## Why PostgreSQL and pgvector?
PostgreSQL supports structured relational data, while pgvector enables vector similarity search within PostgreSQL.

## Why LiteLLM?
LiteLLM provides a common interface for supported LLM providers and can simplify model integration and selection, depending on configuration.

## Important Design Considerations
- Validate user permissions before retrieving sensitive records.
- Enforce tenant isolation.
- Treat retrieved content as data, not trusted instructions.
- Restrict tools to explicitly permitted operations.
- Validate tool arguments and structured outputs.
- Record enough information to investigate failures.
- Evaluate retrieval quality and answer correctness separately.
- Avoid conclusions when supporting evidence is missing.

title: AI Compliance and Financial Operations Assistant — Interview Questions
text:
## Interview Questions
**What problem does this project solve?**  
It helps financial operations and compliance teams investigate transaction information using natural language instead of manually searching records.

**Why is this an agentic system?**  
The application can follow a multi-step workflow, select conditional paths, invoke tools, and process results before producing a response.

**How is it different from a basic chatbot?**  
It can retrieve business data, invoke approved tools, and validate its output against evidence.

**How do you reduce hallucinations?**  
Use relevant retrieval, trusted tool results, deterministic rules, explicit instructions, evidence checks, and evaluation tests. These reduce risk but do not guarantee every answer is correct.

**What happens when evidence is insufficient?**  
The system should say the available information is insufficient rather than invent an answer.

**How would you evaluate it?**  
Use test questions with expected answers and supporting evidence. Measure retrieval relevance, answer correctness, groundedness, tool selection, schema validity, and failure rates.

**What is the difference between a tool and RAG?**  
RAG retrieves relevant information, commonly from a document or knowledge collection. A tool executes a defined operation, such as querying an authorized database or applying a business rule.

## Tell Me About Yourself
I completed my Bachelor's in Computer Engineering from Savitribai Phule Pune University. I have 2.5+ years of experience in software engineering, with a focus on Generative AI and LLM applications.

I have worked on AI-powered applications in fintech and e-commerce, including an agentic RAG system for financial investigations, a product catalog assistant, and document intelligence workflows.

My main technologies are Python, FastAPI, LangGraph, LangChain, LiteLLM, PostgreSQL, and vector search. I focus on building applications that retrieve relevant information, use tools where required, and validate their outputs.

## Explain RAG in Simple Words
RAG means Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Before answering a question, the application searches its knowledge base for relevant information and gives that information to the LLM as context. For example, a portfolio chatbot can search my resume and project documentation before answering questions about my experience.

title: Interview Questions and Answers — What Is Agentic AI? … What Is the Difference Between RAG and Fine-Tuning?
text:
## What Is Agentic AI?
Agentic AI refers to AI applications that can work through a task using defined steps, tools, and decisions rather than generating only one response. An agent might classify a financial question, retrieve transaction data, call an approved tool, and use the results to prepare an answer.

## What Is the Difference Between RAG and Fine-Tuning?
RAG provides relevant external information to the model at inference time. Fine-tuning changes model parameters through additional training. RAG is often useful when information changes frequently or must be retrieved from private documents. Fine-tuning is useful for adapting model behavior or task performance when the training approach and data support it.

title: Interview Questions and Answers — What Is the Difference Between LangChain and LangGraph? … What Is Hallucinat
text:
## What Is the Difference Between LangChain and LangGraph?
LangChain provides components for building LLM applications, such as prompts, retrievers, and tool integrations. LangGraph provides orchestration for stateful, multi-step workflows with conditional transitions. They can be used together.

## What Is the Difference Between an LLM and an Embedding Model?
An LLM generates or interprets language. An embedding model converts text into numerical vectors for similarity search. Some model families offer both generation and embedding capabilities, but the tasks are different.

## What Is Hallucination?
Hallucination occurs when a model generates information that is unsupported or incorrect. It can be reduced through relevant retrieval, explicit instructions, constrained outputs, tool-based data access, validation, and evaluation. Adding RAG does not eliminate it.

title: Interview Questions and Answers — How Do You Evaluate a RAG Application? … How Do You Handle Incorrect Structu
text:
## How Do You Evaluate a RAG Application?
I create test questions with expected answers and relevant source documents. I evaluate whether retrieval finds the correct information, whether the answer is supported by that information, and whether the final output is correct and useful. I also test missing-information cases and irrelevant retrieval results.

## What Is Grounding?
Grounding means linking a model's output to reliable information available in the application. For example, a clinical extraction system can retain the source page and text supporting an extracted value.

## How Do You Handle Incorrect Structured Output?
I validate the output against a schema. If validation fails, the application can retry with appropriate error information or route the case for review. Even when schema validation succeeds, I separately check whether the content is correct.

title: Interview Questions and Answers — What Is Function Calling? … What Is Prompt Injection?
text:
## What Is Function Calling?
Function calling lets a model request an operation using a defined function and structured arguments. The application executes the function only after validating the arguments and checking permissions.

## What Is Prompt Injection?
Prompt injection is an attempt to manipulate an AI application through instructions embedded in user input or retrieved content. Mitigations include treating retrieved documents as untrusted data, restricting tool permissions, validating inputs, and separating model-generated decisions from authorization checks.

title: Interview Questions and Answers — How Do You Prevent an Agent from Calling the Same Tool Repeatedly? … How Do
text:
## How Do You Prevent an Agent from Calling the Same Tool Repeatedly?
I inspect the execution trace and identify repeated calls, their arguments, and returned results. I check whether the workflow lacks a stopping condition, tool errors cause repeated retries, or the agent fails to use previous results. Possible fixes include limiting iterations, validating arguments, detecting repeated calls, adding stop conditions, and testing against a regression dataset.

## How Do You Choose Between an LLM and a Traditional ML Model?
I consider the task, data, expected accuracy, latency, cost, and output requirements. For stable classification tasks with sufficient labeled data, a traditional model may be more predictable and economical. An LLM may be more useful when contextual interpretation or varied inputs are important. A hybrid approach can use rules or traditional models for straightforward cases and an LLM for ambiguous cases.

title: Interview Questions and Answers — How Do You Debug Poor Retrieval? … What Is the Difference Between Latency an
text:
## How Do You Debug Poor Retrieval?
I inspect the original documents, text extraction, chunking, metadata, embedding model, query, and retrieved results. I test changes individually and compare retrieval metrics on a representative dataset.

## What Is the Difference Between Precision and Recall?
Precision measures how many retrieved or predicted items are relevant or correct. Recall measures how many of the relevant or correct items were successfully retrieved or identified. The exact interpretation depends on the task and evaluation setup.

## What Is the Difference Between Latency and Throughput?
Latency is the time taken to complete an operation or request. Throughput is the number of operations or requests processed during a period.

title: Interview Questions and Answers — How Do You Make an AI Application More Reliable? … How Do You Explain a Tech
text:
## How Do You Make an AI Application More Reliable?
I use input validation, appropriate retrieval, controlled tool access, schema validation, source-grounding checks, automated tests, evaluation datasets, monitoring, and human review for uncertain cases.

## How Do You Handle Missing Information?
I distinguish between what the available evidence supports and what is unknown. If evidence is insufficient, I state the limitation rather than inventing a value.

## How Do You Explain a Technical Project to a Nontechnical Person?
I explain the problem first, then what the application does, how it helps the user, and how success is measured. I introduce technical details only when they help explain the solution.

title: Project Decisions and Engineering Reasoning — Purpose … Why Use Structured Outputs?
text:
## Purpose
This document records reasoning behind technical decisions in my projects. The answers below describe general engineering principles relevant to my projects. They should not be interpreted as records of specific experiments unless those experiments were actually performed.

## Why Use RAG Instead of Sending Every Document to an LLM?
RAG retrieves relevant information instead of requiring the application to include every document in each request. It can reduce unnecessary context, improve access to relevant evidence, and support larger knowledge collections. The best approach depends on document size, retrieval quality, context limits, cost, and latency.

## Why Use Structured Outputs?
Structured outputs make model responses easier to validate and process programmatically. A clinical extraction workflow might require fields such as test name, value, unit, and date. The schema must match the application's requirements, and factual validation remains necessary.

title: Project Decisions and Engineering Reasoning — Why Use Deterministic Validation Alongside an LLM? … Why Use a W
text:
## Why Use Deterministic Validation Alongside an LLM?
An LLM is useful for interpreting language and context, but it may generate incorrect values. Deterministic checks are better suited to enforce rules such as required fields, allowed formats, valid dates, and known constraints. A combined approach uses the LLM for interpretation and application code for explicit rules.

## Why Use a Workflow Graph?
A graph can make complex AI workflows easier to control. Nodes can handle classification, retrieval, tool execution, validation, and response generation. Conditional transitions allow the workflow to choose the next step based on the current state. For simple tasks, a single model call may be sufficient.

title: Project Decisions and Engineering Reasoning — Why Use Hybrid Retrieval? … Why Keep Tools Restricted?
text:
## Why Use Hybrid Retrieval?
Vector search can retrieve conceptually similar information, while lexical search can retrieve content with matching terms. Hybrid retrieval can combine these strengths, especially when a query contains descriptive language and exact names or identifiers. Confirm benefits using a representative evaluation dataset.

## Why Include Human Review?
Human review is useful when the application encounters ambiguous evidence, conflicting values, low-quality OCR, or high-impact decisions. The system should identify uncertain cases and provide source information for the reviewer.

## Why Keep Tools Restricted?
An AI application should not receive broader permissions than it needs. Tools should validate arguments, enforce authorization, and limit operations to approved actions. Sensitive actions should not depend solely on the LLM's judgment.

title: Project Decisions and Engineering Reasoning — How Should a New AI Feature Be Evaluated? … How Should Model Cos
text:
## How Should a New AI Feature Be Evaluated?
1. Define the task and expected behavior.
2. Build a representative test dataset.
3. Establish baseline performance.
4. Select metrics that match the task.
5. Test normal cases, edge cases, and failure cases.
6. Review incorrect outputs.
7. Change one major factor at a time where practical.
8. Compare results against the baseline.
9. Keep regression tests for previously solved failures.

## How Should Model Cost Be Reduced?
Potential methods include choosing a suitable model for each task, reducing unnecessary context, caching repeated results where appropriate, limiting redundant tool calls, and using smaller models for simpler tasks. Evaluate each optimization against quality, latency, reliability, and total operating cost.

title: Project Decisions and Engineering Reasoning — How Should Latency Be Reduced? … How Should Production Readiness
text:
## How Should Latency Be Reduced?
Potential methods include profiling the workflow, reducing unnecessary sequential model calls, optimizing retrieval, caching suitable results, and running independent operations concurrently where safe. Measure actual latency before choosing an optimization.

## How Should Hallucinations Be Investigated?
1. Identify the exact question and incorrect response.
2. Inspect retrieved context and tool outputs.
3. Check whether the required evidence was available.
4. Determine whether the failure came from retrieval, interpretation, generation, or validation.
5. Add a targeted test case.
6. Apply a specific fix.
7. Re-run the test and broader regression suite.

## How Should Production Readiness Be Assessed?
Consider correctness, security, authorization, error handling, observability, performance, scalability, cost, data privacy, and recovery from failures. A successful demonstration is not enough to establish production readiness.

title: Project Decisions and Engineering Reasoning — How Should Metrics Be Reported?
text:
## How Should Metrics Be Reported?
Metrics should be tied to a defined measurement method, test dataset, and evaluation period. A retrieval-quality claim should specify the baseline, evaluation questions, relevance criteria, and metric used. If a metric has not been measured, describe it as a target or expected benefit rather than an achieved result.

title: Technical Skills and Interview Reference — Python … Prompt Engineering
text:
## Python
Python is my primary language for backend development and AI applications. Common use cases include API development, document processing, retrieval pipelines, data validation, and LLM integration.

## FastAPI
FastAPI is a Python framework for building APIs. It can receive requests, validate inputs, execute processing workflows, and return responses.

## LLMs
Large Language Models generate and interpret text based on the input and context provided. They are useful for summarization, structured extraction, classification, question answering, and tool selection. Their outputs can be incorrect, so important results should be validated.

## Prompt Engineering
Prompt engineering involves designing instructions and context to guide model behavior. A useful prompt defines the task, expected output, constraints, and how to handle missing information.

title: Technical Skills and Interview Reference — Structured Outputs … Vector Search
text:
## Structured Outputs
Structured outputs constrain a model's response to a predefined format, such as JSON. They simplify downstream processing, but values still need factual validation.

## RAG
Retrieval-Augmented Generation retrieves relevant information and provides it to an LLM as context for generating a response. A typical workflow includes document processing, chunking, embeddings, indexing, retrieval, and answer generation. RAG does not guarantee factual correctness.

## Embeddings
Embeddings represent text as numerical vectors, allowing systems to compare text based on semantic similarity and retrieve related information.

## Vector Search
Vector search systems store or index embeddings and retrieve items based on similarity. pgvector enables vector operations in PostgreSQL. FAISS is a library for efficient similarity search over vectors.

title: Technical Skills and Interview Reference — BM25 … MCP
text:
## BM25
BM25 is a lexical retrieval method that ranks documents based on query-term relevance. It can work well when exact terms, names, codes, or product identifiers matter.

## Hybrid Search
Hybrid search combines multiple retrieval approaches, such as vector similarity and BM25. Results can be combined using a ranking strategy such as Reciprocal Rank Fusion.

## LangChain
LangChain provides components and integrations for LLM applications, including model interfaces, retrievers, prompts, and tools.

## LangGraph
LangGraph supports stateful workflows with nodes, conditional edges, and controlled transitions. It is useful for multi-step AI applications requiring explicit orchestration.

## LiteLLM
LiteLLM provides a common interface for supported model providers and can help applications integrate multiple models consistently.

## MCP
The Model Context Protocol defines a standardized approach for connecting AI applications with external tools and data sources.

title: Technical Skills and Interview Reference — Function Calling … RAGAS and TruLens
text:
## Function Calling
Function calling allows a model to request execution of a defined function or tool using structured arguments. The application validates the request, enforces permissions, executes the operation, and returns the result.

## Guardrails
Guardrails reduce risks such as invalid inputs, unsafe outputs, unsupported claims, and unauthorized tool use. They may include schema validation, permission checks, content checks, and deterministic rules.

## LLM Evaluation
LLM evaluation measures how well an AI application performs on defined tasks. Metrics may include correctness, groundedness, answer relevance, retrieval quality, schema validity, and tool-selection accuracy.

## RAGAS and TruLens
RAGAS and TruLens are tools and frameworks used to evaluate aspects of LLM applications and RAG pipelines. Their metrics and integrations differ; they are not the same product. Interpret scores according to metric definitions and evaluation data.

title: Technical Skills and Interview Reference — LangSmith … AWS
text:
## LangSmith
LangSmith supports tracing, debugging, evaluation, and monitoring workflows for LLM applications.

## OCR
Optical Character Recognition converts text in images or scanned documents into machine-readable text. OCR output can contain errors, especially with poor image quality, handwriting, or complex layouts.

## Pydantic
Pydantic validates data using defined models and types. It is useful for API requests and structured model outputs.

## PostgreSQL
PostgreSQL is a relational database for structured application data. It can also support vector search through pgvector.

## Docker
Docker packages applications and dependencies into containers for consistent execution across environments.

## Kubernetes
Kubernetes orchestrates containers and supports deployment, scaling, networking, and application recovery.

## AWS
AWS provides cloud infrastructure and managed services. Relevant services include S3 for object storage, SQS for message queuing, and EKS for managed Kubernetes.

title: Technical Skills and Interview Reference — Technical Problem-Solving Approach
text:
## Technical Problem-Solving Approach
I identify required behavior and failure cases, choose the simplest suitable solution, implement validation, test representative scenarios, inspect failures, and improve the system based on evidence.
